step1_analysis.description: A Gilbert-cell based XOR/XNOR gate used as a lock detector or phase detector. It employs Current Mode Logic (CML) with a differential pair tree and source follower output buffers.

paper_reference.title: A 39-to-45-Gbit/s Multi-Data-Rate Clock and Data Recovery Circuit With a Robust Lock Detector

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the lock detector circuit

sky130_expected.calculation: Tail current ~0.5mA (set by VCS=0.8V and R_tail=200), two source followers ~0.5mA each. Total current ~1.5mA. Power = 1.5mA * 1.8V = 2.7mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on typical CML bias currents in 130nm to achieve >1GHz operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Tail current 0.5mA steered into 1kOhm load gives 0.5V single-ended swing, or 1.0V differential.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for 1.8V CMOS supply and typical CML load resistors.

propagation_delay.description: Delay from input crossing to output crossing

sky130_expected.calculation: RC delay at the internal nodes. R=1k, C_parasitic~20fF. Delay ~ 0.69*R*C ~ 15-30ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS 130nm is slower than InP HBTs, so delay will be larger.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to verify XOR/XNOR logic function, measure differential output swing, propagation delay, and power consumption.
